A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same survey. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and references support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 synthesizes findings from cited studies without reporting original experiments, simulations, user studies, or empirical data analyses.

after.justification: v2 remains a literature survey. Table 1 and Figure 2 document literature-selection counts rather than empirical research findings. Figure 4 contains adapted examples, and the added TCD performance result is explicitly attributed to Yao et al.

M1.justification: The four-stage mitigation taxonomy is retained, and neither version proposes an original model or training algorithm. Added descriptions of ALUM, BSR, LAAT, and TCD concern cited methods, not changes to an author-proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or benchmark evaluation. The benchmark inventory in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 5 retains the same tasks and datasets, including multimodal benchmarks. Added literature-search sources are not additional model-evaluation datasets.

E2.justification: There is no evaluated comparator set in either version. Additional methods discussed in Section 4 are literature coverage, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: No executed evaluation protocol changes. Retained benchmark descriptions preserve settings such as SCORE's ten prompts and five sampling runs at temperature 0.7. Figure 6 supplies recommendations rather than an implemented testing protocol.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 4 adds qualitative failure cases involving prompt variation, jailbreaks, fairness, and spurious sentiment cues, with representative inputs and outputs. These are adapted illustrations of reported behavior, not new ablations or author-run robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports statistical uncertainty for original empirical results. Descriptions of repeated sampling and consistency measurement in surveyed benchmarks remain unchanged; no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-reporting practices appear.

E6.justification: v2 Section 4.2 newly reports Yao et al.'s TCD result of up to a 39% absolute gain for smaller models. Table 1 and Figure 2 also add literature-selection counts: 508 identified, 337 screened, and 209 included. However, Table 1's screened rows sum to 331. These additions do not establish a same-setting improvement by this paper.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.2 adds explicit mathematical objectives and variable definitions for ALUM, C-AdvUL/CAPO, BSR, and LAAT, extending v1's predominantly verbal treatment. These are formulations of surveyed methods; no original theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same substantive text and contributions: defining robustness, organizing its sources and mitigation strategies, reviewing evaluation tools, and identifying research challenges. Positioning text moved into the introduction largely repeats v1's Discussion.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies older classifier regularization results as conceptually transferable to generative LLMs, revises Section 3.2.1's ERM-centered explanation toward next-token prediction, and adds metric-to-mitigation recommendations in Figure 6. The main robustness trade-offs and future-work limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Section 1.1 documents six search sources, the January 2020–June 2025 publication window, a representative query, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and backward snowballing. This improves disclosure of the survey process but does not establish changes to model-training settings or introduce reproducible experimental code.

R1.justification: v2 expands cited coverage of adversarial training, regularization, alignment, backdoors, and bias, including ALUM, BSR, LAAT, TCD, and Qi et al. It also replaces the sDPO description with Segment-Level DPO and removes much of the former Discussion's comparison with related surveys. The overarching research positioning remains.

P1.justification: Section 2.2 is extensively rewritten from nested lists into seven subsections, parts of Section 4.2 are substantially expanded, and a search-methodology section is added. The standalone Discussion is removed with some framing relocated to the introduction, and duplicated closing prose is shortened.

P2.justification: v2 adds a search-count table, PRISMA diagram, failure-example panel, mitigation decision matrix, and practitioner-guidance flowchart. It removes v1's tree illustration and redraws the interdependence and lifecycle diagrams. Existing source, metric, and benchmark tables are retained under new numbering, with some layout corrections.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency and usability through search documentation, explicit mathematical explanations, applicability qualifications, and practical guidance. These gains are tempered by inconsistent screening totals in Table 1, unexplained thresholds in Figure 6, and ambiguity between the stated exclusion of VLM work and retained multimodal coverage. The revision provides a limited net improvement to the largely unchanged survey.
